html:
South Africa is the country at the southern tip of Africa. It was formed in 1910 as the Union of South Africa, became a republic in 1961, and held its first election open to all races in 1994.

For most of the century a white minority ruled. Land laws such as the Natives Land Act of 1913 kept most land for whites. From 1948 the National Party built apartheid, a full system of racial separation.

  • 1960: police killed 69 protesters at Sharpeville; the African National Congress was banned.
  • 1961: a republic, outside the Commonwealth.
  • 1976: the Soweto uprising of schoolchildren.
  • 1990: Nelson Mandela freed after 27 years in prison.
  • 1994: the first democratic election; Mandela became president.

The Truth and Reconciliation Commission then heard the crimes of the apartheid years. Gold and diamond mining made it Africa's most industrial economy.
sum: South Africa is the country at the southern tip of Africa. It was formed in 1910 as the Union of South Africa, became a republic in 1961, and held its first election open to all races in 1994.
